prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universally “best” Miami personal injury lawyer — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case, your goals (quick settlement vs. trial), budget, and preferences (language, communication style, etc.). I can help you find the best match. First, here’s how to pick a top car-accident lawyer and what to look for.

Key qualities to look for
- Substantial car-accident/personal-injury experience (years and number of similar cases).  
- Trial experience and a track record of settlements/verdicts — important if insurer won’t pay fairly.  
- Resources to investigate the crash (accident reconstruction, medical experts).  
- Good communication: timely responses and a clear point of contact.  
- Contingency-fee arrangement (most PI lawyers work on contingency) and clear explanation of costs.  
- Strong reputation: client reviews, peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell, AVVO), and no disciplinary history with The Florida Bar.  
- Local knowledge of Miami-Dade courts and insurance practices.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?  
- Who will handle my case — the attorney or staff?  
- Do you try cases or mostly settle? What percent go to trial?  
- What is your contingency fee and what costs will I owe if we don’t win?  
- How do you estimate value for my case? How long might it take?  
- Can you provide recent client references or outcomes for similar cases?

Where to check credentials and reviews
- The Florida Bar (for license status and discipline).  
- Martindale-Hubbell, Google reviews, local court records for case results.  
- Miami-Dade Bar Association or local referral services.  
- Ask for recent verdicts/settlements and client testimonials.

Red flags
- Pressure to sign quickly without explaining options.  
- No clear fee agreement or evasiveness about who will handle the work.  
- Poor communication or unwillingness to put things in writing.  
- Unrealistic guarantees of a specific result.

If you’d like, I can:
- Build a short list (3–5) of well-rated Miami car-accident lawyers or firms with phone numbers, website links, and recent results; or  
- Help you prepare for consultations by drafting a short script and checklist.

If you want that list, tell me: the date of the accident, severity of injuries, whether the police report exists, whether you’ve talked to insurers, and any preferences (language, budget, trial-focus).
